observation.visible_scene: A top-down view of a wooden work surface. At left lies a sheet of colored number/symbol stickers, a gray PVC pipe set diagonally, and a small metal cutting tool (scissors-like) in the middle. At right, two hands hold a single iridescent CD/DVD disc by its edges; the disc's central hub carries a small white protrusion. The camera and all background items (pipe, tool, sticker sheet) stay fixed in place throughout.
visible_changes: A small green digit sticker (reading '6') becomes visible at the lower rim of the disc: absent in the first frames, a tiny green sliver appears around frame 4, and it grows into a fully placed '6' sticker by the later frames.

The right index finger moves from the right edge of the disc down to the lower rim to adjust/press the green sticker, then withdraws toward the right in the final frames while the left thumb continues to hold the disc edge.
The hands and disc as a unit drift slightly leftward and upward within the frame over the segment (the background does not move, indicating this is object/hand translation, not camera motion).
The rainbow reflection pattern on the disc shifts orientation as the hands tilt the disc a little; the disc does not visibly spin about its center (the hub protrusion keeps roughly the same angle).
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the green sticker is being freshly peeled from the sheet, already being pressed on, or later removed; what happens before frame 1 and after the last frame.
Whether additional stickers are applied to the disc beyond this excerpt.
uncertain_details: Exact identity of the small metal tool (scissors vs. compass/cutter).
Whether the green piece is a sticker being affixed or a sticker being positioned/peeled; its precise shape is partly occluded by the thumb early on.
The small apparent size/position change of the disc may be a slight tilt rather than a true translation; relative hand-disc geometry is held constant.
